lines.text: Day eight. Eight hours later, that door is the only reason you're two thousand feet up.
And the woman behind it has a question you can't answer.
lines.cap:
AND SHE HAS A QUESTION
YOU CAN'T ANSWER.

lines.text: Her name is Priya. Coastguard radio. Nine years.
She found you by tracking your transmissions. That should have worried you more than it did.
Rule one. A Sea King burns six hundred kilos of fuel an hour.
lines.cap:
RULE 1. A SEA KING BURNS
600 KILOS AN HOUR.

lines.text: The airfield's tanks are full. She can fly it. You fill it to the brim.
lines.cap:
THE TANKS ARE FULL. SHE CAN FLY.
YOU FILL IT TO THE BRIM.

lines.text: Rule two. Every kilo you load costs you range.
Water, twenty kilos. Map, nothing. Radio, three. Food, sixty-one.
You leave the food. All sixty-one kilos. Food exists at the rig. Range doesn't.
lines.cap:
YOU LEAVE THE FOOD. ALL OF IT.
FOOD IS AT THE RIG. RANGE ISN'T.

lines.text: Rule three. Range is the only thing keeping you alive.
lines.cap:
RULE 3. RANGE IS THE ONLY
THING KEEPING YOU ALIVE.

lines.text: Rig Bravo. Four hundred miles of open water. No land between.
Eleven forty. Two thousand feet over the sea, she finally says it.
lines.cap:
11:40 AM. 2,000 FEET UP,
SHE FINALLY SAYS IT.

lines.text: Then she says the other thing. Who have you been talking to on that radio?
lines.cap:
“WHO HAVE YOU BEEN
TALKING TO ON THAT RADIO?”

lines.text: You look at the crank handle. Day one. Day three. Day five. You only ever listened.
You have never spoken into it.
